concept.title: Categories not yet in a group
concept.shortdesc: These categories sit alone in the clustering hierarchy, so the grouping step named no group for them. A person deciding the final structure would place each one.

conbody.note: Draft group. Groups are a convenience for browsing the draft: the hierarchy was proposed by a second clustering pass and named by a language model, and no person has reviewed it.

ul.li: : Serving personnel, reservists, cadets, veterans and their families or dependants.
: Women and ladies of any age or background, including women's groups and women with higher levels of need.
: People experiencing menopause or perimenopause and their partners, along with related women's health issues such as pelvic floor weakness.
: People eligible through being registered with a GP in a named area or scheme, together with NHS staff and a few NHS-related groups.
: People with obsessive-compulsive disorder or closely related conditions (such as body-focused repetitive behaviours), along with their partners, parents and loved ones.
: People who take part in a sport or game and welcome players of any age, skill or experience level, from beginners to experienced.
: Lesbian, gay, bisexual, trans, non-binary and queer people, including young people and their friends, partners or family.
: People interested in gardening, plants, allotments and green activities.
: People who find it hard to move around, because of disability, illness, age or risk of falls, including wheelchair users.
: Mothers and families who are breastfeeding or wish to breastfeed, including those combination feeding or expressing.
: Deaf people and people with hearing loss, tinnitus or NHS hearing aids, including those needing hearing aid care.
: People who enjoy crafts such as embroidery, knitting and lace, from complete beginners to experienced makers.
: Businesses of any size or stage, including start-ups, self-employed people and business owners, as the audience for support.
